posts.caption:
Quick quiz 👇 This tax bill went up $420. Which line did most of it: A) County, B) School or C) Municipal?

Drop your guess in the comments, then swipe for the answer.

In this made-up example, one line explains 57% of the increase. That tells you where to look first. It doesn't mean the bill is wrong: your assessment notice and local tax rates explain why a line changed.

Try the free property-tax example at ifyoumind.com. No account needed.

Illustrative example with made-up figures. Not tax advice.

#propertytax #homeowners #taxbill #personalfinance #budgeting #financialliteracy #moneytips #homeownership

media.alt_text: Quiz slide with made-up figures: "This tax bill went up $420. Which line did most of it?" Three choices: A, County. B, School. C, Municipal. Swipe for the answer.
Same home, two years, made-up figures: total property tax was $4,200 in 2024 and $4,620 in 2025, up $420, about 10 percent.
The answer is B, School. Increase by line in the made-up example: County plus $90, School plus $240, Municipal plus $90. $90 plus $240 plus $90 equals $420.

School tax was 57.1 percent of the $420 increase in this made-up example. That shows where to look first. It does not show the bill is wrong; an assessment notice and local tax rates explain why it changed.
Find the line that moved. Explore the free property-tax example at ifyoumind.com. No account needed for the example.
